english: I've lost my wallet
use: Tell a friend, staff or the police box (kouban) that your wallet is gone.

example.romaji: yabai, saifu nakushita kamo. doko da?
example.ja: やばい、財布なくしたかも。どこだ？
example.english: Oh no, I think I lost my wallet. Where is it?

examplePolite.romaji: sumimasen, saifu o nakushite shimatta n desu ga.
examplePolite.ja: すみません、財布をなくしてしまったんですが。
examplePolite.english: Excuse me, I've lost my wallet.

notes: nakusu is 'lose'; otoshita (dropped it) is just as common.

english: oops, I got it wrong; I made a mistake
use: Admit a slip like a wrong number, train or answer; the -chatta adds an 'oops'.

example.romaji: a, densha machigaechatta. tsugi de oriyou.
example.ja: あ、電車間違えちゃった。次で降りよう。
example.english: Oh, I got on the wrong train. Let's get off at the next stop.

examplePolite.romaji: a, densha o machigaete shimaimashita. tsugi de orimasu.
examplePolite.ja: あ、電車を間違えてしまいました。次で降ります。
examplePolite.english: Oh, I took the wrong train. I'll get off at the next stop.

notes: machigaeru is 'get something wrong'; machigatteru is 'it's wrong'.

english: I won't make it in time; there's not enough time
use: Panic about a train or deadline; ma ni atta is 'made it!'

example.romaji: yabai, kono mama ja ma ni awanai!
example.ja: やばい、このままじゃ間に合わない！
example.english: Oh no, at this rate I won't make it!

examplePolite.romaji: sumimasen, kono mama da to ma ni aimasen.
examplePolite.ja: すみません、このままだと間に合いません。
examplePolite.english: Sorry, at this rate I won't make it in time.

notes: ma ni atte imasu also politely declines: 'I'm fine, thanks, I have enough'.

english: this is a problem; what do I do now?
use: Muttered when you're stuck; someone nearby may offer help: dou shita n desu ka? (what's wrong?).

example.romaji: komatta na, kagi ga mitsukaranai.
example.ja: 困ったな、鍵が見つからない。
example.english: This is a problem, I can't find my keys.

examplePolite.ja: 困りましたね、鍵が見つかりません。
examplePolite.english: This is a problem. I can't find my keys.

notes: Staff offer help with nanika okomari desu ka? (is something wrong?).

english: I overslept
use: The standard excuse for being late in the morning.

example.romaji: gomen, nebou shita! juppun okureru.
example.ja: ごめん、寝坊した！十分遅れる。
example.english: Sorry, I overslept! I'll be ten minutes late.

examplePolite.romaji: sumimasen, nebou shimashita. juppun hodo okuremasu.
examplePolite.ja: すみません、寝坊しました。十分ほど遅れます。
examplePolite.english: Sorry, I overslept. I'll be about ten minutes late.

english: I can't go on; it's hopeless; I'm done for
use: Said when you're exhausted, overwhelmed or think it's all over.

example.romaji: mou dame, ashi ga ugokanai.
example.ja: もうダメ、足が動かない。
example.english: I can't go on, my legs won't move.

notes: dame alone is 'no good' or 'not allowed'; mou adds 'any more'.

english: I can't anymore; no way
use: Give up on food, work or a situation; young people say it about small things too.

example.romaji: mou muri, kore ijou taberarenai.
example.ja: もう無理、これ以上食べられない。
example.english: I can't, I can't eat any more.

notes: muri is 'impossible'; muri shinaide is 'don't push yourself'.

english: I'm at my limit
use: Said when tiredness, stress or patience has run out; heavier than mou muri.

example.romaji: nemukute mou genkai. saki ni neru ne.
example.ja: 眠くてもう限界。先に寝るね。
example.english: I'm too sleepy to keep going. I'm heading to bed.

examplePolite.romaji: nemukute mou genkai desu. saki ni yasumimasu.
examplePolite.ja: 眠くてもう限界です。先に休みます。
examplePolite.english: I'm too sleepy to go on. I'll turn in first.

notes: genkai is 'limit'; you'll hear it about overtime and deadlines too.

english: I'm nervous; I get nervous
use: Before an interview, a speech or meeting someone important; kinchou shiteru is 'I'm nervous right now'.

example.romaji: ashita mensetsu da kara, sugoku kinchou suru.
example.ja: 明日面接だから、すごく緊張する。
example.english: I've got an interview tomorrow, so I'm really nervous.

examplePolite.romaji: ashita mensetsu na node, totemo kinchou shimasu.
examplePolite.ja: 明日面接なので、とても緊張します。
examplePolite.english: I have an interview tomorrow, so I'm very nervous.

notes: Not 'excited': waku waku suru is the happy kind of nerves.

english: what a relief; I feel reassured
use: When news or someone's words remove a worry; tell others anshin shite (don't worry).

example.romaji: kekka, daijoubu datta. anshin shita.
example.ja: 結果、大丈夫だった。安心した。
example.english: The results were fine. What a relief.

examplePolite.romaji: kekka ga daijoubu de, anshin shimashita.
examplePolite.ja: 結果が大丈夫で、安心しました。
examplePolite.english: I'm relieved the results were fine.

english: I'm relieved; phew
use: The sigh when a worry ends: a test passed, someone arrived safe.

example.romaji: buji de yokatta. hotto shita yo.
example.ja: 無事でよかった。ほっとしたよ。
example.english: I'm so glad you're safe. What a relief.

examplePolite.romaji: buji de yokatta desu. hotto shimashita.
examplePolite.ja: 無事でよかったです。ほっとしました。
examplePolite.english: I'm glad you're safe. What a relief.

notes: Close to anshin shita; hotto shita is the instant release, anshin the calm that follows.

english: I feel better; it got easier
use: After medicine, rest or a weight off your mind; also when a task gets easier.

example.romaji: kusuri nondara, daibu raku ni natta.
example.ja: 薬飲んだら、だいぶ楽になった。
example.english: After the medicine, I feel a lot better.

examplePolite.romaji: kusuri o nondara, daibu raku ni narimashita.
examplePolite.ja: 薬を飲んだら、だいぶ楽になりました。
examplePolite.english: I took the medicine and feel much better.

notes: raku is 'ease': raku ni shite kudasai is 'make yourself comfortable'.

english: well, of course; naturally
use: Agree that something is obvious; sorya is a squeezed sore wa.

example.romaji: sorya sou da yo, juu jikan mo aruita n da kara.
example.ja: そりゃそうだよ、十時間も歩いたんだから。
example.english: Well, of course, we walked for ten hours.

notes: Close to sore wa sou, but means 'obviously' more than 'fair point'.

english: that's just how it is
use: Accept or explain something you can't change, often as sou iu mon da yo.

example.romaji: shigoto nante, sou iu mon da yo.
example.ja: 仕事なんて、そういうもんだよ。
example.english: That's just how work is.

examplePolite.romaji: shigoto wa, sou iu mono desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: 仕事は、そういうものですよ。

notes: mon is a casual squeeze of mono (thing).

english: that's true; fair enough
use: Concede a point, often before a but: sore wa sou da kedo...

example.romaji: sore wa sou da kedo, ima wa okane ga nai.
example.ja: それはそうだけど、今はお金がない。
example.english: That's true, but I don't have the money right now.

examplePolite.romaji: sore wa sou desu kedo, ima wa okane ga nai n desu.
examplePolite.ja: それはそうですけど、今はお金がないんです。
examplePolite.english: That's true, but I don't have the money right now.

notes: Online, sore wa sou alone is a stock 'fair point'.

english: just kidding
use: Take back a tease, or a joke someone took seriously.

example.romaji: uso uso, joudan da yo. okotta?
example.ja: うそうそ、冗談だよ。怒った？
example.english: Nah, just kidding. Are you mad?

examplePolite.romaji: joudan desu yo. ki ni shinaide kudasai.
examplePolite.ja: 冗談ですよ。気にしないでください。
examplePolite.english: Just kidding. Don't take it seriously.

notes: uso uso (literally 'lie, lie') is another quick 'just kidding'.

english: just so you know; let me tell you
use: Flags a warning or something you want on record; can sound pushy.

example.romaji: ittoku kedo, watashi wa kankei nai kara ne.
example.ja: 言っとくけど、私は関係ないからね。
example.english: Just so you know, this has nothing to do with me.

notes: Short for itte oku kedo; the polite version is itte okimasu ga.

english: a lot happened, so...; it's a long story
use: Hints at trouble without explaining; listeners usually don't press.

example.romaji: maa, iroiro atte, shigoto yameta n da.
example.ja: まあ、いろいろあって、仕事辞めたんだ。
example.english: Well, a lot happened, and I quit my job.

examplePolite.romaji: maa, iroiro atte, shigoto o yamemashita.
examplePolite.ja: まあ、いろいろあって、仕事を辞めました。
examplePolite.english: Well, it's a long story, but I quit my job.

notes: iroiro is 'all sorts'; iroiro arigatou is 'thanks for everything'.

english: keep it a secret; it's a secret
use: Before or after sharing something private; naisho! alone refuses to tell.

example.romaji: kore, minna ni wa naisho da yo.
example.ja: これ、みんなにはないしょだよ。
example.english: Don't tell anyone about this.

examplePolite.romaji: kore, minna ni wa naisho desu yo.
examplePolite.ja: これ、みんなにはないしょですよ。

src: じゃあ、そういうことで
ja: じゃあ、そういうことで
kana: じゃあ、そういうことで
english: okay, so that's settled; right, let's go with that
use: Wraps up a plan or a call once things are decided, right before saying bye.

example.romaji: jaa, sou iu koto de. mata ashita ne.
example.ja: じゃあ、そういうことで。また明日ね。
example.english: Okay, that's settled. See you tomorrow.

examplePolite.romaji: dewa, sou iu koto de yoroshiku onegai shimasu.
examplePolite.ja: では、そういうことでよろしくお願いします。
examplePolite.english: Right, let's go with that, then. Thank you.
